blocks.text: PLACES YOU SHOULD VISIT IN SHILLONG

content.text: Laitlum as the name suggests literally means “the end of hills” and the name does give justice to this mesmerizing great canyon. This beautiful hilltop is located in the East Khasi Hills of Shillong. The grand canyons are a visual treat to one’s eyes. The scenic beauty of this place outgrows everyone’s expectations. Nature has placed one of its priceless gems in Shillong. Several tourists and photographers are in awe of the picturesque beauty here that do not wish to leave this place. The green wide pastures invite you to take a walk on them and experience nature at its closest and get a view of the depth of the canyons.

Shillong is known as the East of Scotland, and the ideal place to get a magnificent view of the city is Shillong Peak. Located at 2000 meters above sea level, this claims to be the highest point of this beautiful city. On a clueless day, you can expect to get a clear vision of the Himalayan Range and the Bangladesh Plains.

This is one of the popular places in Shillong. It is a lesser-known fact that the radar station of the Indian Air Force is located here, due to which tourists are required to show Identity Card to maintaining security etiquettes.

Ward’s Lake is named after Sir William Ward, who was the Chief Commissioner of Assam. The idea of creating a lake struck him first so in honor of that the lake is named after him. You will be surprised to know that the lake was dug out by a Khasi prisoner named Jismot Chyme. The local authorities have highly maintained this lake. you can head to the bridge over the lake and enjoy feeding the fish or indulge in other recreational facilities like Paddle Boating.

Also known as the THREE STEP WATERFALL, this falls breaks up into three steps. This tourist spot is sure to give you peace from within because of its enchanting beauty. During the colonial period, the British had given the name Elephant Falls as the lowest rock on the fall resembled an elephant. The summer season is a great time to visit this place. Since it is located 12kms away from the city, this waterfalls is one of the major tourist hubs in and around Shillong.

Located amongst the hills of Meghalaya this scenic man-made reservoir was made on the same day that Shillong was given birth. It is the first hydel project to take place in the Northeast of India. The flora and fauna at this lake is worth exploring.

Indulge in the local delicacies while you shop to your heart’s content. This famous market simultaneously portrays both traditional and modern selling methods. You name anything and be sure to find it here, from food, electronic items, garments to winter wear, bakeries, grocery items, and gadgets.

The travel time from Guwahati Airport to Shillong is around 3 hr 13 min(115.1 km) via NH6. However, if you want to stop for tea-sipping, you can stop at local tea shops of Nongpoh, which is the mid-way from Guwahati Airport to Shillong.
